accepted.name: arbitrum_decoded_events_clean
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  BLOCK_HASH AS block_hash,
  BLOCK_NUMBER AS block_number,
  TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(BLOCK_TIMESTAMP) AS block_timestamp,
  TRANSACTION_HASH AS transaction_hash,
  TRANSACTION_INDEX AS transaction_index,
  LOG_INDEX AS log_index,
  ADDRESS AS address,
  EVENT_HASH AS event_hash,
  EVENT_SIGNATURE AS event_signature,
  TOPICS AS topics_variant,
  ARGS AS args_raw,
  REMOVED AS removed,
  -- expose first three topic values (if present) for easy filtering/joining
  TRY_CAST( (CASE WHEN TOPICS IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN ARRAY_SIZE(TOPICS) >= 1 THEN TOPICS[0]::STRING ELSE NULL END) AS VARCHAR) AS topic_0,
  TRY_CAST( (CASE WHEN TOPICS IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN ARRAY_SIZE(TOPICS) >= 2 THEN TOPICS[1]::STRING ELSE NULL END) AS VARCHAR) AS topic_1,
  TRY_CAST( (CASE WHEN TOPICS IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN ARRAY_SIZE(TOPICS) >= 3 THEN TOPICS[2]::STRING ELSE NULL END) AS VARCHAR) AS topic_2
FROM GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_ARBITRUM_ONE_US.DECODED_EVENTS
accepted.description: Normalized/clean projection of GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_ARBITRUM_ONE_US.DECODED_EVENTS with canonical aliases, typed timestamps, and extracted topics flattened metadata. Use this as a stable normalized base when analyzing decoded events (preserves keys for joins to logs/transactions). | Use for: Count events by signature or address over time; Filter decoded events by specific topic values or event_signature; Join decoded events to logs/transactions to enrich with transactional metadata

  TRY_CAST( (CASE WHEN "topics" IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN ARRAY_SIZE("topics") >= 2 THEN "topics"[1]::STRING ELSE NULL END) AS VARCHAR) AS topic_1,

FROM GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_ARBITRUM_ONE_US.LOGS
accepted.description: Normalized projection of GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_ARBITRUM_ONE_US.LOGS exposing canonical column names and topics variant for downstream parsing and joins with decoded events. | Use for: Join logs to decoded events via transaction_hash+log_index to enrich logs; Filter logs by address/topic and compute counts over windows; Detect reorgs via removed flag

accepted.name: cronos_transactions_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t."transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  t."transaction_index" AS transaction_index,
  t."block_hash" AS block_hash,
  b."block_number" AS block_number,
  t."block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  t."from_address" AS from_address,
  t."to_address" AS to_address,
  t."value" AS value,
  t."gas" AS gas,
  t."gas_price" AS gas_price,
  b."miner" AS miner,
  b."gas_limit" AS block_gas_limit,
  b."gas_used" AS block_gas_used
FROM GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_CRONOS_MAINNET_US.TRANSACTIONS t
LEFT JOIN GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_CRONOS_MAINNET_US.BLOCKS b
  ON t."block_hash" = b."block_hash"
grain: one row per transaction enriched with block info
accepted.description: Denormalized view joining transactions with their block metadata from GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN.GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_CRONOS_MAINNET_US to provide one row per transaction enriched with block-level fields. Useful when analyzing transaction values, fees, or miner attribution on Cronos. | Use for: Compute gas or fee statistics per miner or per block; Analyze transaction value distributions over time; Correlate transaction-level metrics with block-level metrics

accepted.name: arbitrum_events_rank_latest_per_tx_log
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  block_hash,
  block_number,
  block_timestamp,
  transaction_hash,
  transaction_index,
  log_index,
  address,
  event_hash,
  event_signature,
  args_raw,
  removed,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY transaction_hash, log_index ORDER BY block_number DESC, block_timestamp DESC) AS rn
FROM arbitrum_decoded_events_clean
grain: one row per decoded event occurrence with a rank (rn) per transaction+log
accepted.description: Assigns a deterministic rank per (transaction_hash, log_index) ordering by block_number and block_timestamp to pick the latest appearance/version of an event. Useful to deduplicate events across reorgs or pick the most recent event state per log slot. | Use for: Select latest non-removed event per log (WHERE rn = 1 AND removed = false); Detect event duplicates or reorg-induced replacements
